cases.refreshed: Need help with 3D printing or looking for guided, hands-on experience? This personalized one-hour session at the Almaden Branch offers step-by-step support from a trained volunteer to assist you with 3D printing. This session is ideal for beginners seeking practical experience, guided support, and confidence in using 3D printing technology. This is also a good opportunity for those who attended our 3D Printing workshop and now want to try their hands at it. Participants will have the opportunity to print a simple model under supervision. If you do not have a design, you may choose one from Thingiverse. Personal designs must be in. Stl format and will be printed using PLA filament. All designs must be compatible with the Creality K1C printer and have a print time of under 45 minutes. Final approval of printability will be determined by the program lead. By appointment only. One appointment per quarter per person. For questions, please call (408) 808-3040 or send an email to ab.sjpl@sjlibrary.org This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Almaden Branch Library

cases.refreshed: Learn to design in Tinkercad and see your creation come to life with our 3D printer! Each class introduces a new technique in Tinkercad or other 3D design tools. Participants will have the opportunity to create a project which will be printed out for pick up later. Classes are on the second Saturday of the month, except in June and October, when it will be on the third Saturday. No experience necessary, participants do not have to participate in all sessions. May 9 - Magnets (negative space + combining shapes) June 20 - Stamps (scribble tool + rotation) July 11 - Standing Sculptures (alignment + supports) August 8 - Free Choice (importing and editing outside designs) September 12 - Hinged Shapes (hinges + print in place) October 17 - Lithophanes November 14 - Cookie Cutters (2D to 3D conversion) December 12 - Snowflakes (codeblocks for generating designs) Appropriate for ages 8+ - younger children will need to be accompanied by an adult to assist them with their design. One dedicated helper needed per child under 8. Space is limited - tickets will be available at the desk 30 minutes before the program begins. One ticket per participant, helpers/spectators do not need a ticket. Each person participating must be present in order to receive their ticket. There are two sessions, one at 3:30 and one at 4:45 pm, to help with crowding. These sessions are identical.

She creates and presents educational based programs that are also fun.

events.title: Sounds of South Asia: an exhibit

cases.refreshed: This interactive photography exhibit showcases several musical instruments from the South Asian subcontinent. Each exhibit will have a QR code that allows participants to listen to the sound of the instruments performed in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. They include stringed, wind, and percussion instruments passed down from generations, which are still performed around the Bay Area. Come and enjoy this exhibit which starts on November 14, 2026, closing on December 5, 2026 The exhibit is brought to you by the South Asians in Silicon Valley initiative at the SJSU King Library. Through this unique initiative, the SJSU King Library records, preserves, and shares the living legacy of the South Asian diaspora in the San Francisco Bay Area. Website: https://library.sjsu.edu/sasv
